newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom is world No 4 telecoms co.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom is world No 4 telecoms co.

text.p: France Telecom, France's main telephone operator, is coming to the market with a 30 to 50 billion franc Initial Public Offer (IPO) in May with share trading scheduled to start on June 9.
Following are key details (all figures are for 1996)
WHAT: World's number four telecoms operator and Europe's number two after AT&T Corp, Nippon Telegraph and Telecom Corp and Deutsche Telekom.
NET PROFIT: 2.1 billion francs after non-recurrent charges, 14.5 billion francs excluding these one-off exceptionals.
CAPITAL STOCK: One billion shares of 25 francs nominal.

MANAGEMENT BOARD: Michel Bon, chairman and chief executive officer, Pierre Dauvillaire, resources including finances, Jean-Francois Pontal, Jacques Champeaux, Jean-Yves Gouiffes and Jean-Jacques Damlamian.

AREA OF BUSINESS: Fixed-network and mobile telecommunications services for business and private customers; leased lines, data transmission, online computer services, television uplink and transmission services, cable television networks, pagers, equipment sales and rentals and satellite capacity marketing.
INTERNATIONAL ACTIVITIES: networks in 22 foreign countries. Atlas joint-venture with Deutsche Telekom and Global One alliance which also includes Sprint Corp.

MAIN COMPETITORS: Cegetel, unit of Generale des Eaux with British Telecom Plc, Mannesmann AG and SBC Communications. Bouygues Telecom of Bouygues and Italy's STET. Smaller rivals in leased lines and business services.
There is already competition in France in mobile telecommunications while fixed line communications will be opened up in January 1998.

REGULATION: Since January 1, the Autorite de Regulation des de Telecommunications (ART) regulates market with the aim of promoting fair competition in 1998. ART to publish late March or early April a list of interconnection charges. France Telecom will remain responsible for basic telecoms in France -- phone booths, emergency calls, connections to remote areas -- with other operators having to contribute to the costs.

STATE INVOLVEMENT: French government will keep a 51 percent stake and all current France Telecom staff can keep their status as civil servant if they wish, with state pension guarantee. France Telecom to make a one-off 37.5 billion franc payment to the government after which the state will pay out the pensions. France Telecom to make "normal" pension contributions annually.
